subject: Logic
title: Limits of Thought Experiments
description: A micro-lesson that makes Limits of Thought Experiments usable.

hook.text: A thought experiment proved the Earth must be flat—if it were round, people on the bottom would fall off. Oops.

buildup.text: Thought experiments are only as good as the assumptions they start with. Bad premises yield confident nonsense.

discovery.text: They can't replace empirical data when the question involves how the physical world actually behaves.

twist.text: Many thought experiments generate contradictory conclusions depending on which intuition you favor.

climax.text: Use them to clarify concepts and test assumptions—not as substitutes for measurement and observation.

punchline.text: Logic without facts is a beautiful trap.

quiz.question: What is a key limitation of thought experiments?
options: They depend on assumptions that may be wrong
